subject: Next steps: data sovereignty checklist & export constraints
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps: data sovereignty checklist & export constraints

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps:

- SOC 2: you asked whether Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. Short answer: yes — our Type II report is current (covering controls through 2025). I've attached a one-page summary. Full report available under NDA; happy to coordinate.

- Data residency: Acme needs EU data residency for patient-identifiable workflows. Redwood offers EU-hosted inference endpoints in our Frankfurt region for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private deployments can be provisioned in EU on request.

- Cross-border/export controls: You called out OFAC/ITAR screening and export control constraints. Our legal team confirmed we perform OFAC screening on customer accounts and have export-control policies; ITAR typically applies to defense-related models/data — please confirm whether any Acme workload is ITAR-controlled.

- HIPAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workflows via Private deployments and BAAs. We can share our template BAA and security artifacts once you indicate interest.

Immediate asks / next steps we agreed on:
1) Acme to confirm whether any datasets or models are ITAR-restricted (reply to this thread).
2) Acme to kick off the vendor security questionnaire — I attached the VSA PDF; please return with answers and any evidence.
3) Redwood to share SOC 2 summary (attached) and a short EU-region latency/availability note (Marcus will add technical specifics).

I'll also open a short HubSpot ticket and a DocuSign route if you want the SOC2 NDA. If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-min follow-up with our security engineer.

Best,
Naomi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Redwood.pdf (fillable), SOC2-TypeII-summary-2025.pdf

Subject: Re: Next steps: data sovereignty checklist & export constraints

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- ITAR: Acme does not handle ITAR-controlled technical data in the clinical AI group; we do have a separate defense division, but that's out of scope for this evaluation. So for clinical workloads ITAR should not apply.

- HIPAA & BAAs: yes, we will need a BAA for any PHI workloads. Please loop in your privacy counsel or provide the template.

- OFAC: we run entity-level screening for vendors; happy to share our vendor list if you need it.

We'll start filling out the Vendor Security Questionnaire this week. Procurement copied — can you confirm an expected turnaround for the questionnaire once returned (i.e., typical review SLA)?

Also, can you confirm whether the EU-hosted endpoints are physically isolated (customer tenancy) or multi-tenant? Latency to Frankfurt is a key metric for our performance team.

Regards,
Sam Taylor
Head of Clinical AI | Acme Health
sam.taylor@acmehealth.com

Hi Sam —

Quick answers to the technical points:

- EU-hosted endpoints: For our hosted plan, we deploy in a regional multi-tenant cluster (Frankfurt eu-central-1) with logical separation and strong tenant isolation (network, IAM, and customer-specific keys). For Dedicated or Private deployments we can provide single-tenant capacity in the EU data center. If you need a formal tech note I can export our regional architecture doc.

- Latency: Typical p50/p95 token latency to eu-central-1 from major EU metros is included in our public perf deck; I ran a quick internal check — average server-side p95 is ~35ms for short-chat sequences. App-level latency will vary based on network; if you'd like, we can run a joint perf test from your infra.

- OFAC & export screening: We enforce OFAC checks at account creation and for billing entities; we also block exports of models/data to sanctioned jurisdictions. For specific export-control regimes (ITAR/EAR), we rely on contractual controls — as Naomi noted, ITAR typically depends on customer data classification.

Action items from engineering side:
- I'll prepare a short "EU deployment technical note" and attach it to the thread.
- If Acme returns the questionnaire, we can typically complete an internal review in 3 business days for standard SaaS use-cases; dedicated/private setups may need longer (5-7 business days).

Thanks —
Marcus
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
